paper_metadata.title: A 4MB On-Chip L2 Cache for a 90nm 1.6GHz 64b SPARC Microprocessor D. Wendell, J. Lin, P. Kaushik, S. Seshadri, A. Wang, V. Sundararaman, P. Wang, H. McIntyre, S. Kim, W. Hsu, H. Park, G. Levinsky, J. Lu, M. Chirania, R. Heald, P. Lazar, et al.

references.sentence: The CPU architecture is discussed in further detail in [1,2] and the CPU characteristics are summarized in Fig. 3.6.1.
The clock (clk at CPU rate) is distributed to the data cache memory array edge and to the Tag/LRU arrays horizontally (Fig. 3.6.2).
The select signals SD, SR, and SW control decode,read and write, respectively; and they are adjusted in half-cpu clock increments (Fig. 3.6.3).
Bitlines are clamped for low swing, allowing transition from sense data to opposite data without intervening precharge signals (Fig. 3.6.4).
Static sense amplifier stages (Fig. 3.6.5) are used in the memory array, as well as for analog, low-level-signal, and global data output paths.
Each sub-array maintains column-redundant elements for a way (column) group of four bitlines (Fig. 3.6.6 note 4 sections per cluster).
